candidateOriginals.title: Jésus donnant les clefs à saint Pierre
candidateOriginals.institution: Musée du Louvre; deposit Musée Ingres-Bourdelle, Montauban
candidateOriginals.scopeAndEvidence: Original signed 1820, reworked 1841–42; Louvre official record. Matthew 16:18–19 keys, not John 21 feeding sheep.

candidateOriginals.title: The Entry of Christ into Jerusalem
candidateOriginals.institution: Indianapolis Museum of Art at Newfields
candidateOriginals.scopeAndEvidence: Museum-indexed original oil canvas circa 1617; Christ on donkey and palm bearers; museum site blocks automated content fetch, corroborated by Google Arts & Culture museum partner.

candidateOriginals.title: The Baptism of the Eunuch
candidateOriginals.scopeAndEvidence: 1626 oil on panel. Institution-supplied research documentation identifies collection object ABM s380; seek current custodian image before comparing its reproduction. Acts 8:26–39.

candidateOriginals.title: The Baptism of the Eunuch
candidateOriginals.scopeAndEvidence: Circa 1660 signed-monogram oil on canvas original; formal official collection record. Not the Rembrandt painting; separate physical object.

candidateOriginals.title: Saint Philip Baptizes the Eunuch
candidateOriginals.scopeAndEvidence: 1748 signed oil-on-canvas overmantel, housed in Beuning Room. Original physically distinct from Rembrandt and Salvator Rosa.

candidateOriginals.title: Saint Paul Shipwrecked on Malta
candidateOriginals.scopeAndEvidence: Circa 1630 original French oil painting. Official museum describes Acts 28:1–6 viper biting Paul on Malta AFTER shipwreck; not a representation of the vessel sinking. Subject match qualified.

candidateOriginals.title: Moses Receiving the Law on Mount Sinai
candidateOriginals.institution: Parliamentary Art Collection, Palace of Westminster
candidateOriginals.scopeAndEvidence: 1784 original monumental oil canvas 548.6 × 373.3 cm, collection data syndicated through Art UK; exactly depicts receiving the Law, not breaking tablets.

candidateOriginals.title: Moses Receiving the Tablets of the Law
candidateOriginals.scopeAndEvidence: 17th-century oil canvas, multiple sequential Sinai and Golden Calf scenes; gifted 2013. Distinguish Hans III Jordaens from Jacob Jordaens. Nîmes syndicated collection data and photographer credit © Florent Gardin.

candidateOriginals.title: The Sacrifice of Elijah Before the Priests of Baal
candidateOriginals.scopeAndEvidence: Circa 1621–22 original, possibly preparatory sketch for larger work, explicitly showing divine fire and Priests of Baal; not an Elijah fed by ravens or an Assumption of Elijah.

candidateOriginals.title: Visión de Ezequiel: la resurrección de la carne
candidateOriginals.scopeAndEvidence: 1630 signed oil canvas 177 × 205 cm; independently attested in Prado's artist encyclopedia, conservation and loan records. The original object page is intermittently blocked, so links to these official corroborations provided.
